<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**8** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/action.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/action.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/action.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/action.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 107d2e8497270aad611f77a81bc341f48c6d3e00` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c9678091016d7406225783f61a9aa6af25d5bc7b` — the merge of head `635bb5a7ab0681bf71396c424ae17e67c4f5031e` into base `107d2e8497270aad611f77a81bc341f48c6d3e00`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c9678091016d7406225783f61a9aa6af25d5bc7b && git checkout c9678091016d7406225783f61a9aa6af25d5bc7b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 107d2e8497270aad611f77a81bc341f48c6d3e00 635bb5a7ab0681bf71396c424ae17e67c4f5031e && git checkout -B drift-repro 107d2e8497270aad611f77a81bc341f48c6d3e00 && git merge --no-ff 635bb5a7ab0681bf71396c424ae17e67c4f5031e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 107d2e8497270aad611f77a81bc341f48c6d3e00
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e05528a7b257b4200779c7ba88cdd9ba240051c4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts + ui/packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts

Inputs read: card #34391 (body and all 8 comments), PR #34500 (body, file list, net diff against merge-base `e8cba8fe`), the check-runs on the head, and the cited code in the tree at the head (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/ActionResultDialog.tsx`, read, not reviewed). The rest of the diff (the two test files, the changeset body, the reference page, the strictness counts, the dropped-refinements baseline, the liveness ledger and its counts) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Check-runs on the head, at the time of reading: 65 runs, no failure. Completed green: Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Lint and Repo Gates and every Lint shard, Type Check · source gates, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Check Documentation Links, Dogfood Regression Gate. PENDING (in progress, no verdict yet): Build Core, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check UI, Lint UI, Build and E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Test UI 1/16 to 16/16. This record does not stand in for those: the spec test suite, the workspace type-check and the UI type-check (the one the `ActionRunner.ts` edit exists for) have not answered on this head, and the seat reads them before landing.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set, field `format` on `resultDialog.fields[]` and `preflight.fields[]`: five members become six (`table` added). Widening. Right.
- Accept-set, new key `columns` on the shared row (`actionAnswerFieldRow`), an array of strict `{ path, label?, format? }`. Before this head the strict row refused `columns` as an unknown key (it is in no alias map), so the key is a pure addition. Right.
- New refusals, all four reachable only through the new value or the new key: `columns` without `format: 'table'` (custom, at `columns`); `table` without `columns` or with `[]` (custom, at `columns`); `table` as a cell format (invalid_value, own message); `table` as `resultDialog.format` (invalid_value, own message). `resultDialog.format: 'table'` and a row `format: 'table'` were both `invalid_value` before, so no input that parsed on `main` is refused here, and the row's `superRefine` adds issues only and transforms nothing, so the parsed output of every old input is unchanged. The changeset's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` sentence is right.
- The dialog-level set and the cell set are derived with `.exclude(['table'])` from the one `z.enum`, no second list. The custom `error` returns undefined for any input but `table`, so an unknown format keeps the generic enum refusal (pinned). Right.
- Public type surface: `resultDialog.format` stays the five-member set in the published types and in the reference page; the row's `format` gains `table`; `columns` is new. `ResultDialogFieldSpec.format` in `@object-ui/core` widens with it, `ResultDialogSpec.format` does not. Right.
- No export added or removed in `@objectstack/spec` (`ActionAnswerFieldFormatSchema`, `ActionAnswerTableColumnSchema` and the two helpers are module-private). Right.
- JSON-schema projection: the row rule is value-dependent and does not project; the baseline records 24 new dropped sites (2 paths in 12 published schemas). Named, generated, not reviewed.
- Liveness: `columns` and its three children are `planned`, the describe opens with the repo's `[PLANNED — not yet rendered]` marker, and the claim behind it is true in the tree: `ResultField` computes `safeFormat` as `table` and has no branch for it, so a `table` field draws its label and no value. Right.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` minor matches what the diff publishes: an added enum member and an added optional key, nothing removed, nothing that parsed now refused. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is on the PR body and in the changeset, with `Metadata-protocol: added` on both, as the card asked. `@object-ui/core` patch for a type-only derivation that changes no runtime path is acceptable; the exported `ResultDialogFieldSpec.format` type widens by one member, which is the point of the edit and is named in the changeset. Check Changeset is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question 1 (route the contract review): answered by this record.
- Open question 2 (keep the `ui/` type derivation in this PR): A, keep. The seat amended the file surface on the card (6932171004), the edit is two type members and no renderer, and deriving from the contract is the root fix rather than a sixth hand-written member. The card's "no console change" line is about the renderer, which this PR does not touch.
- Deviation, R5 wording follows the sibling: verified against the tree. The dialog filters out a field whose path does not resolve, and `ResultField` degrades `code-list` on a non-array to `json`; the `table` bullet says the same for a missing and a non-array value. Accepted.
- Deviation, `columns: []` refused with the missing-list message: right; an empty list draws no column, and the message's fix applies as written.
- Deviation, dropped-refinements baseline +24: accepted, see ①.
- Deviation, the forced probe change in `action-preflight.test.ts` (`table` to `chart`): right; `table` is now a member, the assertion is unchanged.
- Out-of-scope finding, carrier #33187: between this PR and the renderer, an author who writes `format: 'table'` gets a parse-clean action whose value is not shown at all (not even the `json` fallback). It is declared (`planned`, the marker, the changeset), no shipped action uses it, and #33187 is blocked on this card, so it is accepted here; the seat should hold #33187 to re-grading the ledger rows `live` in the same PR.
- `Skills-docs: none`: accepted for the reason given. The hand-written prose list of five formats in `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx` is outside this diff and belongs with the renderer half as well.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts` against the card (asks 1 to 6), ruling A on #33187 as the card quotes it, and its first consumer (`ResultField`, shared by the result dialog and the preflight panel):

- Asks 1 and 2 hold. One row builder still serves both surfaces, the column reuses the row's alias map where it applies, and the key name `columns` collides with nothing on the row.
- Ask 3 holds. Each refusal lands on the key the author must change, carries a message that names the fix, and the "refuse, never default to the element's keys" decision is stated with its reason in the refinement's doc and in the `columns` describe. Attempts to break it: `columns` with no `format` under a dialog-level default (refused, correctly, since the default can never be `table`); an unknown `format` beside `columns` (the enum refusal fires and the row check does not run, one issue, correct); a column alias (`key`, `title`, `render`) answers with the canonical name; `table` nested in a cell is refused by name. None broke.
- Ask 4 holds for the field-level cases (missing value, non-array value, `[]`, column order, header) and matches the sibling formats' behaviour in the tree. It does not hold cleanly for the cell:

S1 (should-fix) — The cell rule of the `table` renderer contract is stated in two ways that a renderer can honour differently, and is silent on the first consumer's commonest case. (a) The `resultDialog` doc says a cell "draws in the column's `format` (omitted: a scalar as `text`); a cell whose value is an object or an array ... draws as compact JSON text", which reads as unconditional: an object or array cell is compact JSON whatever its `format`. The column's own `format` describe, the ledger note and the refusal message ("Drop `format` (... compact JSON text), or write `format: 'json'`") tie that clause to an OMITTED format. Under the first reading a cell `format: 'code-list'` (which needs an array) and a cell `format: 'json'` on an object can never draw as declared, so two accepted values would parse clean and never be honoured, which is the outcome this same change refuses for `columns`; under the second they draw. (b) Nothing says what a cell draws when the column's `path` is absent from that row's element. The per-row answers this format exists for (`alreadyPending`, `notApplied`, a refusal reason present only on refused rows) make that the normal case, not an edge. (c) Nothing says what a cell draws when its declared `format` does not fit the value (`secret` on a number), where the field-level sibling degrades to `json`; and "every cell of an element that is not an object draws as compact JSON text" does not say of what (the element, presumably, repeated in each column). The card asks for a contract "short enough for one console renderer to honour it exactly"; as written #33187 has to choose. Fix in the `resultDialog` doc bullet, with the column `format` describe kept in agreement: say that the object-or-array rule applies when the cell `format` is omitted (or say it is unconditional and narrow the cell set to match), that an absent cell value draws an empty cell, and what a mismatched cell format degrades to. Prose only; no accept-set change is needed if the "omitted" reading is the intended one.

- N1 (nit) — the doc of `actionAnswerScalarFormat` ends "`subject` names the slot in the refusal", but the parameter is `tableRefusal` and carries the whole message. Stale sentence.
- N2 (nit) — the row's `format` describe is still "Per-field format override." and the `table` bullet of the renderer contract carries no planned note of its own; an author meets the `[PLANNED — not yet rendered]` marker only on `columns`. Since `table` cannot be written without `columns`, the marker is reached, so no effect on the contract.

`ui/packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts` against the contract: `SpecResultDialog` and `SpecResultDialogField` are read off the action's input type, so `ResultDialogFieldSpec.format` is the six-member set and `ResultDialogSpec.format` the five-member default set, each comment says exactly that, and the first consumer's `FieldFormat` already derives from `ResultDialogFieldSpec['format']`, so the dialog-level default stays assignable to it. The code agrees with the contract. `ResultDialogFieldSpec` does not carry `columns` yet; nothing reads it on this head, and #33187 adds it with the renderer. The UI type-check that proves the derivation is PENDING on the head (see above).

No must-fix. S1 is open on this head and earns a delta review of its fix; N1 and N2 may ride with it or be left as accepted deviations.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `635bb5a7ab0681bf71396c424ae17e67c4f5031e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts + ui/packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts

Delta review. The previous at-tier record is comment 6932322404, a pass on head `e05528a7b257b4200779c7ba88cdd9ba240051c4` with S1 open and nits N1, N2. Inputs read: that record, card #34391 (body and all 8 comments), PR #34500 (body, comments), the check-runs on the new head, the diff between the two heads restricted to the PR's 11 files (4 files moved, +28/-18), the net diff's file list against merge-base `d4c0c121`, and the cited code in the tree at the new head (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/ActionResultDialog.tsx`, `packages/spec/scripts/build-docs.ts`, `packages/spec/scripts/check-generated.ts`, `.github/workflows/lint.yml`; read, not reviewed). Main's own files that arrived with the merge are not judged.

Check-runs on the new head, at the time of reading: 45 runs, no failure. Completed green (12): Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, Dogfood Regression Gate, Plan Test Core shards, Plan Test UI shards, filter, Auto Label. Skipped (9): the opt-in and queue-only jobs. PENDING (24, in progress, no verdict yet): Build Core, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · CI, release and engine gates, Lint · repo and tooling gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, and the three scoped Lint jobs (tooling self-tests, slot lookup and corpus, query-options erasure). Not yet created on this head: the Test UI shards, Type Check UI, Lint UI, Build and E2E UI. This record does not stand in for any of them. Two matter to this delta in particular and the seat reads them before landing: Test Core (it carries `scripts/strictness-ledger.test.ts`, the pin this head changed, and the 47-case table test) and Type Check · source gates (it runs `check:docs`, the gate on the generated reference page, and the strictness-ledger count check).

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set: unchanged between the heads. The whole of the `action.zod.ts` delta is one JSDoc paragraph on `actionAnswerScalarFormat`, the `table` bullet of the `resultDialog` JSDoc, the text of one refusal message, and two `.describe()` strings. No schema call, key, enum member, alias map or refinement moved. No document changes its parse result, and no parsed output changes. The first clause of the changed refusal message (the part the tests pin) is untouched, and neither test file under `src/ui/` moved.
- The strictObject count going 12 to 13 is not a new closed object on this head. `action.zod.ts` holds 13 `strictObject(` call sites on BOTH heads (lines 239, 375, 865, 931, 943, 995, 1184, 1831, 1907, 1930, 1962, 2101, 2307 at the new head; the same thirteen, one line higher up, at the old). The thirteenth is `ActionAnswerTableColumnSchema`, the column row, which the previous record already judged as a pure addition: it refuses unknown keys only inside `columns`, a key that did not parse before this PR. Nothing the old head accepted is refused on the new one. Only the pin moved; it stays inside the declared widening line and the `Metadata-protocol: added` line.
- The committed ledger count agrees: `docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.counts/ui.md` already read `action.zod.ts` 13 on the old head. Its movement on this head (sites 222 to 224, passthrough 4 to 6, `bulk-action.zod.ts` 4 to 6) is main's #34267 arriving through the merge. Against main at the merge-base (223 sites, 212 strict, `action.zod.ts` 12) the head reads 224 and 213 and 13: exactly this PR's one strict site.
- `strictness-ledger.test.ts`: one assertion value changed (12 to 13) and two comment lines were added beside the earlier moves; no other assertion was touched. 13 is the honest count of the tree at the new head. It was also the honest count at the old head, so the pin of 12 there was false against that tree and the spec suite, pending when the previous record was written, could not have answered green on it. Right fix, and the only forced one.
- Generated faces: `content/docs/references/ui/action.mdx` rightly did not move. The page renders nested shapes for `Action.resultDialog` and `Action.preflight` and shows `fields` as one inline type; it has no shape for a field row or a column, so the row `format` describe and the column `format` describe are not on the page at either head (neither old nor new wording occurs anywhere in the tree outside `action.zod.ts`). The descriptions it does carry (`resultDialog.format`, `resultDialog.fields`, `preflight.fields`) did not change. Its gate is `check:docs` in Type Check · source gates: PENDING. `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` rightly did not move: no refinement was added or removed.
- JSON-schema projection: the two describes change `description` strings in the built schema tree (a build output, not committed). Descriptive only.
- Liveness: two notes in `packages/spec/liveness/action.json` reworded (`columns.path`, `columns.format`); statuses unchanged (`planned`), state counts unchanged. Spec property liveness is green on the head.
- Public surface: no export added or removed, no type changed.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from the previous record and still right: `@objectstack/spec` minor for an added enum member and an added optional key, `@object-ui/core` patch for the type-only derivation. The delta is prose, a refusal-message text, a test pin and regenerated counts; it publishes nothing that would raise or lower either level. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` stand on the PR body and in the changeset. The changeset file did not move and did not need to: it states no cell rule, it points at `resultDialog`. Check Changeset is green on the new head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The previous record's boundary answers stand; none is reopened by this delta.
- For the renderer card #33187, read off the unified rule and the tree: (a) a cell whose path resolves to `null` is a present value that does not fit `text`, so it draws the text `null`, not an empty cell. That is what the rule says and it matches the field-level sibling (`getPath` and the `value !== undefined` filter in `ActionResultDialog.tsx`), so it is consistent, but a server that wants an empty cell on rows with no refusal reason must omit the key, not send `null`. (b) The cell test for `code-list` is the contract's (an array of strings); `ResultField` today tests the field with `Array.isArray` alone. The contract is the authority, and #33187 should bring the field branch to it rather than copy the looser test into cells.
- The PR body's restatement of the renderer contract matches the `resultDialog` bullet clause for clause.
- The hand-written five-format list in `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx` remains outside this diff and belongs with the renderer half, as before.
- SQL push-down: not applicable; the delta adds no query.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts`, the cell rule, read in every place the tree states it:

- `resultDialog` doc bullet: a cell reads the column's dot `path` in the element; `undefined` draws an empty cell; a present value draws in the column's `format` (omitted: `text`) when it fits (`qrcode`, `secret`, `text` take a string, `code-list` an array of strings); any value that does not fit, whatever the format, draws as compact JSON text, which is also how `json` draws in a cell; an element that is not an object draws itself as compact JSON text in the first cell, the other cells empty.
- Column `format` describe: omitted is `text`; a value that does not fit the cell's format, whatever it is, draws as compact JSON text; a missing value draws an empty cell.
- The `table` cell refusal message: drop `format` (a cell value that does not fit its format, an object or an array included, draws as compact JSON text) or write `json`.
- Liveness notes: `columns.format` says the same and points at the bullet; `columns.path` says a path that resolves to nothing draws an empty cell and a non-object element draws as compact JSON text in its row's first cell.
- Row `format` describe, `columns` describe, the changeset, the reference page: none states a cell rule, so none can disagree.

Walked against the cases: format omitted and a string, `text`; format omitted and a number, boolean, object or array, compact JSON text; format given and the value fits, drawn as declared (`code-list` on an array of strings and `json` on anything now draw, which the unconditional reading of the old bullet denied); format given and the value does not fit (`secret` on a number), compact JSON text; path resolving to `undefined`, including a path through a missing or `null` intermediate, empty cell; non-object element, the element once, in the first cell. The first consumer's commonest case named by the previous record (`alreadyPending`, `notApplied`, a refusal reason present only on refused rows) now has one answer: the absent key is an empty cell and the booleans draw as `true` and `false`. The old "omitted: a scalar as `text`" clause, which would have had a renderer choose between stringifying a number and degrading it, is gone; a number has one drawing. Two renderers honouring these texts draw the same cells.

S1: closed. Every statement of the cell rule now has the one reading, parts (a), (b) and (c) of the finding are each answered in the bullet, and the describe, the refusal message and the ledger notes agree with it.

N1: closed. The `actionAnswerScalarFormat` doc now names `tableRefusal` and says what it carries.

N2: closed. The row `format` describe marks `table` as `[PLANNED — not yet rendered]` and says it requires `columns`.

N3 (nit, new) — "an element that is not an object" does not say where an array element or a `null` element falls. Read as JSON types, both are non-objects and draw themselves in the first cell; a renderer testing with `typeof` would read paths in an array and find `null` to be an object. A server answer whose rows are arrays under a declared column list is off the format's purpose, so this is an edge, but four words ("a plain object, so not an array and not `null`") would close it. May ride with #33187's renderer PR, which has to pick the test anyway.

`ui/packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts`: did not move between the heads. It renders nothing; it only derives `ResultDialogFieldSpec.format` (six members) and `ResultDialogSpec.format` (five) from the contract, and the reworded rule changes neither set, so the previous record's judgment stands unchanged. The console's `ResultField` still has no `table` branch, so no renderer exists yet to agree or disagree with the cell rule; the `planned` marking says so truthfully. The UI type-check that proves the derivation has not yet been created on this head.

No must-fix, no should-fix.
